To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prevalence of HBV genotype B was significantly higher than that of genotype C in Taiwanese blood donors.

the frequency of HBe antigen positivity was higher and the serum HBV DNA levels were higher among blood donors with genotype B than among those with genotype C infection, and that precore stop codons were common in both genotype B and C infections but that precore C-1865 was rare in genotype C.

HBV genotype C infection is more pathogenic than HBV genotype B infection and that precore stop codons and precore C-1846 strains are more prevalent than C-1858 precore strains in Taiwanese HBV carriers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the virological characteristics and pathogenesis of HBV genotyping in blood donors.
the clinical and viirological aspects of blood donors infected with hepatitis B virus genotypes B and c.
the clinical and virovlogical aspects of blood donors infected with genotype B or C HBV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HBV genotype B is predominant in Taiwanese blood donors, but HBV genotype C is associated with a higher HBV DNA level and a higher frequency of HBV e antigen positivity than HBV genotype B.
HBV genotype B has a higher frequency of precore mutation and lower serum HBV DNA levels than genotype C, and genotype C infection has a higher frequency HBeAg positivity than genotype B infection.
HBV genotype C is associated with higher HBV DNA level and HBeAg positivity, and the precore mutation is common in HBsAg carriers, irrespective of the HBV genotypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the virological characteristics are different among HBV genotypic strains and that the virologic characteristics of genotype B and C are distinct in the blood donors in Taiwan.
genotype C has a more aggressive course than genotype B.
HBV genotypes have different virological characteristics, but not different clinical features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HBV genotype C is more likely to cause chronic hepatitis B than HBV genotype B, and precore stop codons are common in HBV carriers with HBeAg negativity, irrespective of HBv genotypes.
HBV genotype C has a greater tendency to become chronic and to have a higher serum HBv DNA level than HBV genotype B, but the precore C- 1858 strains are less common.
HBV genotype C has a greater propensity for chronic infection and higher viral replication.
